objective: Falsify or retain whether public aggregate Medicare provider+service data can replace rights-cleared claim-level auditing for duplicate claim identifier detection. No customer data, no outreach, no contract execution.

source_signals.buyer_signal: nonbinding market research; no right to private claims
FedRAMP/comparable security authorization and managed operations requirements are not evidenced
historical independent validation purchase, later termination/deobligation; public USAspending UI strong incumbent

frozen_test: Two authored micro-claim worlds have two services for one beneficiary on separate dates, with identical provider, service, amounts and every named aggregate; one world has unique claim IDs, the other repeats an ID. Only their claim ID differs. Private exact-ID check distinguishes; no public-aggregate-only procedure can distinguish.
comparators: ordinary claim-level exact ID database check when authorized and supplied
public CMS browsing and basic grouping with no claim IDs

acceptance.stopping_rule: execute one frozen pair and adversarial tests once; no post-hoc changes to worlds/projection/requirements on a failure
acceptance.economic_admission: no-deploy absent current rights-cleared input, specific buyer acceptance/contract, complete costs, native-account cash authority and independently observed demand

safety: Synthetic identifiers only, no CPT descriptors, no patient/provider data, no paid API, no outreach; source metadata is public and is not private claims or buyer agreement.
